verdict.rationale: GitBook documents a RESTful API supporting GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE, and its official MCP server lets agents create and configure sites, open change requests, draft content, edit pages and restructure docs. That covers much of the UI's core authoring surface programmatically, but nothing in the evidence states or demonstrates full API/UI parity. Probes also found no OpenAPI spec at standard paths. missing for 10: an explicit API-UI parity claim or coverage matrix, evidence that admin, branding, analytics, permissions and settings are reachable via the API, a discoverable published API spec, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: This API is RESTful and supports standard HTTP methods like GET, POST, PATCH, and DELETE.
Tools like Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and other MCP clients can use it to create and configure sites, open change requests, draft content, edit pages, and restructure docs.
Write in the editor, drive it from your agent, or sync from Git.
